problemRestated: A user could upload a document and click an unconditional 'Continue to Review' link straight through to /onboarding/review with ZERO gate, reaching a screen that presented review candidates as if the company's state were settled, without contract-model analysis (runContractAnalysis) ever having run. Separately, the documents page's 'Contract analysis' status card's own 'view findings' link pointed at that same review page, whose entire data layer (lib/onboarding/review.ts) had zero awareness of ClaimReviewItem - a real, persisted ClaimReviewItem row was proven invisible there.
scopeDiscipline: No UX redesign. The pre-existing, deliberately-allowed two-step upload-vs-analyze design is unchanged: uploadDocumentAction and runExtractionAction (which also fires runContractAnalysis) remain two separate actions, and app/[companyId]/onboarding/documents/page.tsx's own 'Continue to Review' <Link> is BYTE-IDENTICAL to before this fix - still a plain, unconditional link with no run.status/AnalysisRunStatus/disabled={} guard anywhere near it (verified: tests/onboarding/part-b-recert-auditf3-f6-f7-liveflow-bypass.test.ts's own static-trace assertions about that exact markup still pass unmodified). The gate was deliberately placed downstream instead - see mechanism below - which the task's own charter explicitly allows ('redirect... whichever fits this codebase's existing conventions with the least new surface area') and avoids touching a screen a separate, already-scoped workstream (documents page visibility) owns.

gateMechanism.summary: A new predicate, getAnalysisReadinessForCompany(companyId) (lib/contract-model/analysis/service.ts, exported via lib/contract-model/analysis's barrel), is the single source of truth for 'is this company's current document set genuinely analyzed'. app/[companyId]/onboarding/review/page.tsx (the real, unmodified route a user's 'Continue to Review' click and the documents page's 'view findings' link both lead to) now calls this predicate FIRST, before any of its own extraction-candidate queries, and calls next/navigation's redirect(`/${companyId}/onboarding/documents`) whenever the company is not ready - a genuine server-side block on the actual Next.js route, not a client-side disabled affordance that a direct URL visit could route around.
gateMechanism.statesReused: Reuses AnalysisRunStatus verbatim - no new enum value was added to the Prisma schema. 'Completed appropriately' is defined as status COMPLETED or COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW only, per the phase's own required-invariant wording ('not PENDING/RUNNING/FAILED/absent'). PARTIAL (AUDIT-F3's own status for 'at least one instrument durably failed') is deliberately NOT treated as ready - a partially-failed analysis must not be presented as review-ready contract truth either.
gateMechanism.genuineGapAddressed: AnalysisRunStatus alone cannot express 'this specific run's own documentIds no longer cover every document the company currently has' (e.g. a user analyzes doc A, gets a COMPLETED run, then uploads doc B without re-running). getAnalysisReadinessForCompany closes this by comparing the latest run's documentIds against the company's CURRENT document id set and additionally requiring full coverage - a bypass in the same shape (proceeding past unanalyzed content) but subtler, since a stale COMPLETED run would otherwise still read as globally 'ready'. This is the one place a genuine gap justified inference beyond the raw enum, per the task's own allowance ('unless a genuine gap requires a new value') - no new persisted state was introduced, only a derived comparison.
gateMechanism.emptyCompanyHandling: A company with zero Document rows at all is treated as trivially ready (reason NO_DOCUMENTS) - there is nothing to gate, and blocking it would only interfere with the pre-existing, honest 'No extraction candidates yet' empty state, not close any real bypass.

viewFindingsFix.priorDefect: The 'Contract analysis' status card's 'view findings' link pointed at /onboarding/review, but that page's entire data layer (lib/onboarding/review.ts) had zero knowledge of ClaimReviewItem - a persisted ClaimReviewItem row was provably invisible there (AUDIT-F6's own compounding-defect finding).
viewFindingsFix.fix: Added getClaimReviewItemsForCompany(companyId, opts?) to lib/contract-model/compiler/safe-failure/service.ts - the correct domain owner of the ClaimReviewItem model (co-located with recordClaimReview/resolveClaimReview/checkExplicitSafeFailure, never duplicated into lib/onboarding/review.ts, which stays scoped to the separate ExtractionCandidate model). app/[companyId]/onboarding/review/page.tsx now calls it directly and renders a new 'Contract analysis findings' Card - a real, minimal, additional section (not a new page, not a UX redesign) showing each open ClaimReviewItem's materiality, reasonCode, source document, section reference, sourceEvidence quote, and rationale. Defaults to OPEN_REVIEW status, matching AnalysisRun.reviewItemCount's own definition.
viewFindingsFix.whyNotInLibOnboardingReview: lib/onboarding/review.ts's getReviewProgress/getCandidatesForReview are specifically, correctly scoped to ExtractionCandidate (the older, separate review pipeline) - conflating ClaimReviewItem into those same functions would blur two genuinely distinct domain models and their own progress semantics (e.g. ExtractionCandidate's PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED lifecycle vs. ClaimReviewItem's OPEN_REVIEW/RESOLVED_*/SUPERSEDED lifecycle). The already-committed recertification test's own assertion that lib/onboarding/review.ts contains no 'ClaimReviewItem' string continues to hold and pass - by design, not by accident: that file's job never changed, and putting ClaimReviewItem in the same file would be exactly the kind of unwarranted scope creep this phase forbids.
viewFindingsFix.destinationConfirmedReal: The documents page's own 'view findings' link text ('N open review item(s) · view findings') already points at /onboarding/review - unchanged. Since that route now genuinely renders ClaimReviewItem rows once analysis has actually completed, the link's destination is fixed without touching the link itself.

testEvidence.methodology: Exercises the REAL, literal exported default component (ReviewPage from app/[companyId]/onboarding/review/page.tsx) and the REAL server actions (uploadDocumentAction, runExtractionAction) against real Postgres - never an isolated helper called out of context. next/cache and next/navigation are mocked only for the same reason every other test in this codebase mocks them (no live Next.js request context in vitest); getAnalysisReadinessForCompany's own real Prisma queries run unmocked. ReviewPage's returned React element is inspected with react-dom/server's renderToStaticMarkup to confirm actual rendered HTML content, not merely in-memory state.

case1_bypassBlocked.description: Upload a document, never run extraction/analysis, then call the real ReviewPage() directly.
case1_bypassBlocked.result: getAnalysisReadinessForCompany returns {ready:false, reason:'NEVER_ANALYZED'}; ReviewPage calls redirect('/{companyId}/onboarding/documents') and returns null - it never constructs getCandidatesForReview/getReviewProgress output at all. The prior bypass (reaching a rendered review-looking screen with zero AnalysisRun rows) no longer succeeds.

case2_staleBlocked.description: A company with one already-analyzed (COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW) document uploads a SECOND document without re-running analysis, then calls the real ReviewPage() again.
case2_staleBlocked.result: getAnalysisReadinessForCompany returns {ready:false, reason:'STALE_DOCUMENTS_SINCE_LAST_RUN'} despite a real, completed prior run existing for this company; ReviewPage redirects again. Proves the gate is tied to the CURRENT document package, not merely 'has this company ever completed one run.'

case3_goldenPathWorks.description: The exact same real runExtractionAction a user's 'Run extraction' click invokes is called for the uploaded document (deliberately an undiscovered $6,750,000 Investments covenant, no LLM callers injected, matching this codebase's own live-contract-analysis-app-action.test.ts convention so the deterministic semantic-coverage layer is what must catch it).
case3_goldenPathWorks.result: getAnalysisReadinessForCompany returns {ready:true}; ReviewPage does NOT call redirect and returns a real element; a real, persisted OPEN_REVIEW ClaimReviewItem for the $6,750,000 covenant is confirmed both in Postgres AND in the actual rendered HTML output (renderToStaticMarkup), including the item's own rationale text - the golden path is not merely unblocked, the 'view findings' destination genuinely shows the real finding.

case4_reopensAndRecloses.description: After the golden path, the second (stale) document is itself analyzed via runExtractionAction.
case4_reopensAndRecloses.result: getAnalysisReadinessForCompany returns {ready:true} again and ReviewPage renders without redirecting - confirms the gate is not a one-way trap and correctly re-opens once the current document set is genuinely, fully covered by a completed run.

testEvidence.priorTestStillPasses: tests/onboarding/part-b-recert-auditf3-f6-f7-liveflow-bypass.test.ts (the already-committed Part B recertification test that documented both original gaps) passes unmodified: its 'BYPASS STILL REACHABLE' assertion is about uploadDocumentAction alone leaving zero AnalysisRun rows (still true - upload behavior is unchanged, only downstream navigation is gated); its 'STATIC TRACE' assertion that the documents page's Continue-to-Review link carries no gate token is still true (the gate was deliberately placed on the review route instead, not that link); its ClaimReviewItem-invisible-to-lib/onboarding/review.ts assertion is still true (that file was deliberately left unchanged, since the fix lives in the safe-failure domain service + the review PAGE component instead).

finalDisposition: AUDIT-F6 / FINDING-7: CLOSED. A user can no longer reach /onboarding/review (directly, or via the documents page's unchanged 'Continue to Review' link) in a state that presents contract-model analysis as complete/review-ready unless a real, current AnalysisRun genuinely covers the company's current document set with a COMPLETED or COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW status. The 'view findings' link's destination now genuinely surfaces real, persisted ClaimReviewItem rows rather than a page structurally blind to them. The golden path (upload -> real analysis -> real review, including a document set that grows and must be re-analyzed) is verified to keep working end to end.
